test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 06 Feb 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Don't sit on this bench as __**it is just painted**.__
solution:
The correct answer is** "it has just been painted."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the present tense, so option 4, which uses **"has just been painted,"** is the most grammatically correct choice.
 
• Option 1, **"it had painted just,"** is grammatically incorrect because **"it"** cannot be the subject of the verb** "painted."**
 
• Option 2, **"it was painted just,"** is grammatically correct but does not convey the same meaning as the original sentence. It suggests that someone painted the bench at some point in the past, rather than just now.
 
• Option 3,** "it had been painted just,"** is grammatically correct but uses the past perfect tense, which is not necessary in this context.
 
• The correct answer is option 4.

**Correct sentence**: *Don't sit on this bench as **it has just been painted**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 is incorrect because it uses "had" incorrectly; Option 2 is grammatically correct but does not fit the context; Option 3 uses the past perfect tense unnecessarily.
